sq.q: \(\text{Using the Fourier transform of } f(x)=e^{-|x|}, \text{ evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1+x^2} dx.\)
answer: \(\text{By inverse transform at } x=0: f(0)=1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) ds\)
\(\text{Consider } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & |x| < 1 \\ 0 & |x| > 1 \end{cases}, \text{ its Fourier transform is } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{\sin s}{s}\)
\(\text{By inverse transform at } x=0: f(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) ds\)
\(\text{Since } \frac{\sin s}{s} \text{ is even: } \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds = 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin s}{s} ds = \pi\)

lq.q: \(\text{Find the Fourier transform of the derivative } f'(x) \text{ given that } \mathcal{F}\{f(x)\}=F(s).\)
answer: Step Marks \(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f'(x) e^{isx} dx\) (2) Integrate by parts: let \(u = e^{isx}\), \(dv = f'(x)dx\) (2) Then \(du = is e^{isx} dx\), \(v = f(x)\) (2) \(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left[ f(x)e^{isx} \right]_{-\infty}^{\infty} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) is e^{isx} dx\) (3) Since \(f(x) \to 0\) as \(x \to \pm\infty\), the boundary term vanishes (2) \(\mathcal{F}\{f'(x)\} = -is \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) e^{isx} dx = -is F(s)\) (4)
